pointers.sentence: The new message has the old classes' API but is no instance of them (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).
It is built under a policy, `email.policy.default` unless `policy=` names another, and the policy checks the headers (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.message`).
`BadHeaderError`, deprecated, is now `ValueError` itself, so code that catches it catches the policy's error (`django/core/mail/message.py:BadHeaderError`).
A positional use still works, and warns (`django/utils/deprecation.py:deprecate_posargs`).
A value that is neither empty nor a list or tuple of strings is `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:_send_server_message`).

The handler `django.core.mail.mailers` makes a new backend at each lookup, of the class an entry's `"BACKEND"` names, with its `"OPTIONS"` (`django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler.create_connection`).
Without `using=`, it takes a backend the message holds, given as `connection=`, or else what the deprecated `get_connection` makes (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.send`).

Given no backend's path, `get_connection` makes the `"default"` mailer where `MAILERS` is defined, and otherwise the class `EMAIL_BACKEND` names, with no alias (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:get_connection`).

Without `MAILERS`, `get_connection` also warns "Django 2028 will not have a default mailer. …", unless an old email setting is defined, since such a setting warns of its own (`django/core/mail/deprecation.py:warn_about_default_mailers_if_needed`).
Each warns only when used from outside Django (`django/utils/deprecation.py:warn_about_external_use`).
Since 6.1 `send_mail` refuses `fail_silently=True`, `auth_user=` or `auth_password=` beside a backend given as `connection=` (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:send_mail`).
Older versions ignored them there, the documentation says (`docs/topics/email.txt`).
A subclass that defines a method get_connection, which `send` called before 6.1, now makes `send` raise `AttributeError` (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.send`).
A backend made directly, by calling its class, ignores it, as all did before 6.1, and warns (`django/core/mail/backends/base.py:BaseEmailBackend.__init__`).
An SMTP backend made directly, deprecated too, reads the old settings for what it is not given (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend.__init__`).
So given only a host, it raises `AttributeError` at `EMAIL_PORT`, where 5.2.17 and 6.0.8 read port 25 (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`).

A subclass that defines a connection method, undocumented and no longer called, raises `AttributeError` as it is made (`django/utils/log.py:AdminEmailHandler.__init__`; [Logging](../startup/logging.md)).
`BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware` takes its alias from `BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.using`, also since 6.1 (`django/middleware/common.py:BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.send_mail`).

Unless the mailer's `"OPTIONS"` set `"fail_silently"`, an error in sending is raised from `AdminEmailHandler.emit` to the code that logged the record, since logging does not catch what a handler raises (`django/utils/log.py:AdminEmailHandler.send_mail`).
The `task` decorator turns a module-level function into a `Task`, and `Task.enqueue` hands it to its backend of `TASKS` (`django/tasks/base.py:Task.enqueue`).
Django "does not provide a worker mechanism to run tasks", the 6.0 notes say (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`; [Background tasks: `Task`, `TaskResult` and the task backends](../services/tasks.md)).
The default class, `Task`, takes only its own fields (`django/tasks/base.py:task`).
`Task.__reduce__` now pickles the function's dotted path instead (`django/tasks/base.py:Task.__reduce__`).

| `EmailMessage.attach` | Since 6.0, takes an `email.message.MIMEPart`, which 5.2.17 refused; a legacy `email.mime.base.MIMEBase` is attached with a warning | `django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.attach` |

| `EmailMultiAlternatives.alternatives` | Since 5.2, holds `EmailAlternative` named tuples; a plain tuple appended raises `AttributeError` as the message is built | `django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMultiAlternatives._add_bodies` |
| `EmailMessage.encoding` | Since 6.0, an `email.charset.Charset` there raises `TypeError` as the message is built | `django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage._add_bodies` |

| mixed_subtype, alternative_subtype | Gone in 6.0, unwarned: the undocumented subtypes of a message with attachments, or alternatives; set, they make building it raise `AttributeError` | `django/core/mail/message.py` |
| 5.2's _create_ methods | Gone in 6.0: undocumented, _create_message among them; an override of one is not called | `django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.message` |
| the checks of `MAILERS` | New in 6.1: `"mail.W001"` warns of no `"default"`; `"mail.E001"`, in deployment, fails on a development backend there | `django/core/checks/mail.py` |
